facts: Fort Lauderdale is known as the Venice of America due to its extensive network of scenic inland waterways.
The city was named after Major William Lauderdale, who constructed forts in the area during the Second Seminole War.
Fort Lauderdale Beach features a famous promenade lined with a distinctive white wave wall and brick-paved paths.
Hugh Taylor Birch State Park offers a peaceful tropical oasis right next to the bustling beachfront.
Fort Lauderdale experiences around 3,000 hours of sunshine each year, making it ideal for outdoor activities.
The nearby Bonnet House Museum and Gardens preserves historic architecture surrounded by native coastal habitats and wildlife.
Fort Lauderdale Beach is famous for its crystal-clear ocean waters and soft golden sands.
The International Swimming Hall of Fame, dedicated to aquatic sports history, is located near Fort Lauderdale Beach.
Broward County's coastline serves as an important nesting ground for sea turtles every spring and summer.
Fort Lauderdale hosts one of the largest international boat shows in the world every year.
The historic Elbo Room on the beach became iconic after being featured in the classic 1960 film Where the Boys Are.
Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale is one of the busiest cruise ports in the entire world.
Running along the beach promenade provides stunning sunrise views over the Atlantic Ocean.
The Fort Lauderdale area originally belonged to the Tequesta people before Seminole settlement.
Las Olas Boulevard links downtown Fort Lauderdale directly to the vibrant beachfront district.
The offshore barrier reefs along the beach protect the coast and attract colorful marine life.
Fort Lauderdale Beach regularly earns Blue Wave Beach certification for its cleanliness and safety.
Local coastal waters are home to friendly manatees and playful wild dolphins.
Fresh local seafood, especially Florida stone crab claws, is a popular culinary delight along the coast.
Annual road races along the beachfront draw thousands of passionate runners from around the world.
